Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the data — this is exactly what we need to sketch out two concrete reservation paths. Quick summary from our side (high level):

Conservative path (lower cost, more gradual ramp)
- Warm-start baseline: 40 GPUs (mixed single- and multi-tenant lanes)
- Expected to hit 60% of peak QPS with careful batching and prefix caching
- Ramp: 40 -> 65 in 4 weeks -> review; can add burst lanes for sustained spikes

Aggressive path (lower latency, higher reserved capacity)
- Warm-start baseline: 80 GPUs with dedicated low-latency lanes
- Ramp: 80 -> 120 over 6–8 weeks; prioritized scheduling and per-route autoscale

We will produce a technical sizing attachment that maps QPS/model mix to GPU counts and estimated P95. I attached a draft proposal for procurement with placeholder numbers (redwood-proposal-draft.docx).

Next steps:
- I’ll loop Karhtik for the sizing matrix and he’ll propose a week-by-week activation plan.
- Can we schedule a 30-min call early next week to review the two paths and pick which to quote?

On Fri, Dec 18, 2026 at 01:02 PM neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com> wrote:
> Appreciate the data — this is exactly what we need to sketch out two concrete reservation paths.

Oliver / Maya —

Attaching a concise sizing matrix (redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf) with recommended cluster topologies and the assumptions that went into each bucket. Key recommendations (technical):

- Baseline assumptions: medium LLM (~7B), target P95 < 250ms at steady-state, typical sequence length 64 tokens, business-hours QPS ~450–600 (from your sheet).

- Sizing bullets:
  * Conservative: 40 GPUs (A100-style equivalence) — supports ~300–400 qps with batching and prefix caching; expected P95 ~220–260ms depending on user distribution.
  * Balanced: 65–80 GPUs — comfortable for 500–800 qps, P95 ~180–220ms with per-route lanes.
  * Aggressive: 100–120 GPUs — headroom for bursty growth and multi-model traffic, P95 ~<160ms with low batch sizes.

- Ramp schedule we recommend (practical, minimizes cold-start waste):
  Week 0: Warm-start 40 GPUs (canary on 10% traffic)
  Week 2: Add 25 GPUs (move to 65) and open 25% traffic
  Week 4: Move to 80 GPUs, enable dedicated low-latency lanes for critical routes
  Week 8–10: Scale to 100–120 GPUs based on telemetry and quality regression checks

- Operational fallbacks:
  * Route overflow to hosted Redwood variants for 10–20% of traffic during spikes.
  * Autoscaling windows + burst lanes for predictable events.
  * Canary week with traffic shadowing and repetitive evals to catch quality regressions.

I included explicit math and GPU-to-QPS mapping in the attached PDF. If Quantaforge prefers a steeper front-loaded ramp we can produce a cost delta for 80->120 in 4 weeks vs 10 weeks.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf (4 pages, sizing matrix + assumptions)

—Karthik

Thanks Neha and Karthik — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. We’re comfortable proceeding with the conservative warm-start path but prefer an accelerated ramp cadence:

Proposed commitment (Quantaforge intent):
- Warm-start: 40 GPUs (week 0)
- Week 2: 70 GPUs
- Week 4: 100 GPUs
- Week 8: 120 GPUs (final target)

Please convert the balanced/aggressive configuration into a formal quote and I’ll route it through procurement. We’d like the contract to include:
- Minimum sustained 40 GPU guarantee for months 1–3 with a punchout to scale to 120 as telemetry warrants
- SLA details on latency targets and incident response windows
- DocuSign-ready term sheet (send link)

I can sign off quickly if we get a clean term sheet. DocuSign link to send to procurement: https://docusign.com/QUANTAFORGE-12345
